gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Lumary 4" gimbal lights cannot be controlled locally out of the box: in the Home Assistant forum, misra (Mark) could find only Wi-Fi Lumary 4" gimbals and wanted Zigbee or Z-Wave instead, and zimmer62 (Joe) put ESPHome on his Lumary 4" lights to get the local control he required.
standout_why: ChatGPT's answers already say these are 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi lights, that 'Alexa/Google compatibility does not automatically mean Matter support or full local control', and that the lights need constant power and generally don't work with ordinary wall dimmers. I could not open the cited Lumary pages, the Best Buy pages or the Wayfair page; they rate-limited me (HTTP 429) or timed out every time. So I could not check what those pages say. The only page I opened was a forum thread. It adds named users, plus the detail that someone reflashed the lights with ESPHome, to a point ChatGPT already made in general terms. A finding that would decide the pick, Lumary's own wall dimmer and which gimbal models it works with, is listed under unsourced because I could not open a page for it.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. Any Lumary gimbal works with Alexa or Google through the Lumary Wi-Fi app with no hub. A shopper who needs the lights to keep working without the cloud, or wants Zigbee, Z-Wave or Matter, will not get that from Lumary without reflashing the lights. The point that would decide the pick, whether the lights can be dimmed from a wall switch, is still unverified. The rebuilt page needs it opened on Lumary's own product page before it goes in.

findings.note: Post dated 2025-06-05. In the same thread on 2024-10-06, Joe set the requirement: "It must be locally controlled", with a dumb on/off from the wall switch if Home Assistant is down. Reflashing was his way to get local control. I found no maker statement that the lights offer local control, so read this as a named user's workaround, not a feature.
